title: Private kded6 smoke test proved GTKConfig availability but loaded extra modules

method.system_bus: DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS pointed to a nonexistent socket under the fixture; no host session bus was used.
method.kded6rc: Explicit autoload=false entries for all 36 installed KDED plugins except gtkconfig=true.
method.display: Fresh xvfb-run server; XDG config/data/state/cache and HOME were private.

result.evidence: KDED log shows unrelated modules (timezone, touchpad, hardware, print manager, etc.) started despite explicit autoload=false config. Those modules could not reach a host session bus; the test did not use the real system bus.

limits: This proves that the installed gtkconfig plugin can answer org.kde.GtkConfig.gtkTheme on a private KDED bus, but it does not prove palette export or observer integration.
The KDED configuration did not isolate autoloading as intended; do not repeat this broad launch until the module-loader behavior is understood or constrained.
No kded6rc or GTK settings were written outside the private profile by the probe. The observed timezone readback matches the configured host timezone; no GTK theme or user session was changed.
next: Do not rerun kded6 with broad plugin discovery. Continue the authorized GTK2 gap audit using existing visual/native evidence and isolate any needed GTKConfig experiment at the module/process boundary.
